can be eaten while it is underripe and
crisp.  The astringent varieties are har-
vested while still firm and allowed to ripen
fully and soften.  Astringent persimmons
can ripen off the tree when stored at room
temperature.  Non-astringent varieties
are harvested when they are fully colored
and ripe.  Persimmons are also divided
into two classes by their origin:  Japanese
and American.  Although Japanese per-
simmons exist in both astringent and
non-astringent varieties, they tend to be
less astringent than American.  The most
common variety of persimmon available
in the United States is the Hachiya, an
astringent Japanese persimmon that is
large and acorn-shaped.  A popular non-
astringent Japanese variety is the Fuyu,
which is smaller than the Hachiya and
shaped like a tomato.
